name: @olai/tests
//scripts: Bun hosts the runner. Bun executes `.ts` natively, so there is no tsx, no ts-node and no build step between a step definition and the browser driving it — the `.bin/cucumber-js` shebang says node, and `bun run` executes it with bun anyway (verified in a dev shell with node removed from PATH entirely). That is why the dev shell needs no node: if this ever regresses, the symptom is a `node: command not found` from `bun run test`, and the fix is `bun ./node_modules/@cucumber/cucumber/bin/cucumber.js`, not adding node.
//dependencies: @olai/web for the NAMES it owns and nothing else: the `data-testid` record (support/world.ts), the day arithmetic in clock.ts, and the theme table's attribute, storage key and default. @olai/fonts is the same arrangement one package over — the TYPEFACE table's attribute, storage key and default, imported from the package that owns them rather than from the client that draws them. Each is a contract between two packages that never otherwise meet, and the way that kind of contract breaks is silent — a rename compiles on both sides and shows up as a thirty-second timeout. Importing makes it a type error instead. @olai/format is here for two NAMES on the same terms: `MARKS`, the three fields a record may carry, so the disk assertion that a node is UNMARKED is written against the format's own list rather than three field names this suite would spell alone and quietly stop covering the day a fourth arrived — and `FILE_KINDS`, the table saying which files a served directory is made of, so the sweeps in kinds.test.ts hunt the suffixes the format actually claims rather than a list of them kept here. No BEHAVIOUR is imported from either: these tests drive the client through a browser, not through its modules.
//devDependencies: @olai/log is here for its `./testlib` DECODER only: the readiness signal this suite waits on is a line on the server's stdout, and that line's format belongs to @olai/log — so the thing that reads it back is @olai/log's too, rather than a regex this suite would maintain alone and silently stop matching the day a value needed quoting. playwright is pinned to 1.61.1 — the version of `pkgs.playwright-driver` in the pinned nixpkgs. The npm package ships only the driver's JS; the browsers come from the Nix store via PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH, and the driver refuses a browser build it was not compiled against. A minor-version drift here (kolu's 1.59.0, say) does not fail at install time — it fails at `chromium.launch()` with "Executable doesn't exist", pointing at a path inside the store that is real but wrong. Bump this only together with the nixpkgs pin, never on its own.
